guidance: Four career phases; all ten gender items and ten era dimensions per phase covered. Review statuses concern registered fields only. Formal office, party authority, advisory influence and policy outcomes remain distinct. Legal cutoff gaps and search-only evidence are visible.

rows.Finding / value: Sonia Gandhi (née Maino); born 9 December 1946 in Lusiana, Italy; Indian National Congress; living.
Rajya Sabha member for Rajasthan from 4 April 2024; scheduled term ends 3 April 2030. Re-elected CPP chairperson in June 2024.
President from March 1998 to December 2017; returned in 2019; handed charge to Mallikarjun Kharge on 26 October 2022.
Moved from family-linked public life to party leadership, coalition-building and welfare advocacy, then opposition and senior parliamentary leadership.
First elected from Amethi and Bellary in 1999; later represented Rae Bareli; shifted to Rajasthan’s Rajya Sabha representation in 2024.
Seven direct constituency victories: two in 1999, four subsequent general-election wins and one 2006 by-election. Multiple seats and a by-election are not separate full parliamentary terms.
Declined the premiership in 2004. Congress/UPA leadership and NAC chairmanship gave policy influence; Cabinet rank at NAC must not be confused with a ministerial portfolio.
Helped connect party leadership and civil-society welfare demands through the NAC; food-security advocacy is directly documented. Laws and implementation were collective institutional work.
Electoral revival was followed by organisational weakness and national defeat. Praveen Rai’s account stresses centralisation; that is an interpretation, not proof of a single cause.

Family networks enabled access; foreign-origin challenges complicated legitimacy. Women’s reservation advocacy is documented, but personal prominence alone does not establish women’s empowerment outcomes.

National Herald: cognisance declined in December 2025 without deciding merits; ED challenge still under consideration in the latest October 2026 report. Voter-roll complaint: dismissal set aside and fresh hearing ordered in September 2026.
rows.Research note: No later substantive order confirmed through research cutoff. These are procedural findings, not guilt or exoneration.

rows.Description: Born on 9 December 1946.
Married Rajiv Gandhi in New Delhi; family connection preceded independent party leadership.
After Rajiv’s assassination, established the Rajiv Gandhi Foundation and associated research institute.
Took primary membership of Congress.
CWC appointed her president immediately, replacing Sitaram Kesri.
AICC ratified the appointment; her speech called for organisational renewal.
Institutional indexed account says she could not assemble an alternative government after Vajpayee’s fall.
Offered resignation after three senior leaders challenged her premiership candidacy; CWC rejected it.
Won Amethi and Bellary; party biography identifies Amethi representation and opposition leadership.
Congress formed a coalition government; she declined the premiership and backed Manmohan Singh.
Resigned Lok Sabha membership amid office-of-profit controversy; NAC resignation is corroborated by subsequent correspondence reporting.
Returned from Rae Bareli with 474891 votes.
Left withdrew over the nuclear agreement; Singh government survived a confidence vote.
Congress increased to 206 seats; Sonia retained Rae Bareli.
Government announced Sonia as chairperson with Cabinet rank/status.
Urged parliamentary passage of the food-security legislation.
Congress fell to 44 seats; she retained Rae Bareli.
Rahul Gandhi succeeded her as Congress president.
Returned to the presidency after Rahul’s resignation; retained Rae Bareli.
Transferred party presidency to Mallikarjun Kharge.
Supported reservation and demanded immediate operation and OBC inclusion.
Took oath representing Rajasthan.
Unanimously re-elected CPP chairperson.
National Herald cognisance litigation and voter-roll remand require separate procedural tracking.
